summary: A manual script that sends sample phrases to the Groq AI and prints how it turns each one into a structured task or goal.
purpose: Check how well the AI reads quick-add phrases before users depend on it.
why: Likely reason: testing and tuning the AI instructions outside the app. Reason not stated in the code.
how: 1. Reads the Groq key from the local settings file by hand. 2. Defines a helper that sends a phrase with detailed instructions and asks for JSON. 3. Parses the reply and prints it. 4. Runs four sample phrases one after another.
inputs: Sample phrases written in the script, and the Groq key in the settings file.
outputs: Console printout of each phrase and its parsed result. No files change.
risks: Each run is a paid call to an outside AI service. A reply that is not valid JSON stops the script. The settings reader is a simple pattern that can misread unusual values.
debug: If the script exits with a missing key message, check that the settings file has a Groq key line. If JSON errors appear, print the raw reply first. When results differ from the app, compare this prompt with the one in the server route.
